about: The source of truth for this repository's settings: every value is the safest one that still lets the repository work. collect.ts compares each live reading with this file. Loosening, removing or ungating a setting needs an entry in changes with its reason and issue, which guard.ts checks. The baseline below lists the legitify policies this repository doesn't follow, and why.

settings.why: Private, not internal: an internal repository is open to the whole enterprise. Private Pages also need a private repository
The branch ruleset, CI and the merge rule all assume main
A fork of a private repository copies its code outside these rulesets; with forking off, fork pull request workflows cannot exist either
Wiki edits skip review, the secret scan and the case-word hook
Same as the wiki: an unreviewed place to write
The backlog is the GitHub issues
The Projects page board is linked to this repository
The required dco check needs a Signed-off-by line on every commit; this adds it to commits made on github.com and through the API
Merges are squash only
Merges are squash only
Merges are squash only
Sessions enter the merge queue (#392) through auto-merge; the queue admits a pull request only once its required checks pass on that head. Owner turned it on 2026-11-04
GitHub's update-branch commit has no Signed-off-by line; branches catch up by rebase
A merged branch is gone, so a late push opens a fresh branch instead of reviving a frozen one
The squash commit on main keeps every commit's Signed-off-by line
Free fix pull requests for known vulnerable dependencies
Dependabot alerts are free on private repositories and feed the Security page
A published release's tag and assets can't be changed afterwards. The repository has no releases yet, so nothing breaks
CI and the required checks run on Actions
Only GitHub's own actions and named trusted ones may run
settings.source: legitify all_github_actions_are_allowed; GitHub secure use reference

settings.why: Every action on main is already pinned to a full commit SHA; this makes GitHub refuse one that isn't
settings.source: GitHub secure use reference, pin actions to a full-length commit SHA; REVIEW.md rule 6

settings.why: checkout, setup-node, cache, labeler and upload-artifact, and the Pages actions, are GitHub's own
A verified badge is not a review; third-party actions are named one by one
The only third-party actions on main: claude-code-action and setup-bun, which it calls inside. The wildcard lets Dependabot move a SHA; sha pinning still requires a full SHA
settings.source: Workflows on main; GitHub docs, allowlist syntax

settings.why: Safe and working: every action a workflow on main uses, and every action those call in turn, is allowed and SHA-pinned, so the allowlist never breaks CI
A workflow's token reads unless the workflow asks for more, which review catches
A workflow must never approve a pull request
settings.source: legitify actions_can_approve_pull_requests; GitHub secure use reference

settings.why: claude-review runs only when the CLAUDE_ENABLED variable is true, and a skipped job passes the required check, so review would silently stop. Read from the vars context of a job with no environment, as claude-review sees it, and kept as true or false only
No other repository may call this repository's workflows
settings.source: GitHub docs, sharing actions from a private repository

settings.why: At most 90 days: long enough for each metric to link to its run and for the score history; shorter is safer and fine
An active branch ruleset covers the default branch
Release branches get the same protection as main
settings.source: Ruleset as set by the owner

settings.why: Every commit carries a verified signature
Nothing is pushed to main directly
Merges are squash only
main can't be deleted
main's history can't be rewritten
Squash-only merging already keeps history linear; the rule makes it a guarantee
The two required checks, each from the GitHub Actions app
settings.source: CLAUDE.md, What runs where; legitify requires_status_checks

settings.why: A required check counts only when GitHub Actions reports it, so no other app or token can fake a pass
settings.source: GitHub docs, required status checks with an expected source

settings.why: The merge rule already requires 0 commits behind main; this makes GitHub enforce it
A protected branch can't be created around the checks
settings.source: Ruleset as set by the owner

settings.why: If a person ever approves, a later push dismisses that approval. No approvals are required, so nothing stops
One login opens every pull request and GitHub refuses self-approval, so 1 or more would stop every merge. Quality, speed, consumption and security are measured on their pages
Only the admin role may bypass, and only by merging a pull request, never by a direct push. It is the owner's merge route for a change the review check fails on purpose
No tag is created, moved or deleted except by an admin
settings.source: Ruleset as set by the owner

settings.why: Only the admin role creates release tags
settings.source: Ruleset as set by the owner

settings.why: GitHub itself refuses a push that adds a case store, an export, a case folder or a room's settings, on every branch, before review sees it
settings.source: CLAUDE.md, No case data, ever; .gitignore; GitHub docs, push rulesets

settings.why: The largest tracked file is under 1 MB; a 5 MB cap stops a dropped folder of documents
No one may bypass the case-data push rules; to clean up a leak the ruleset is turned off for that one push, as SECURITY.md says
Every environment, and so every secret kept in one, deploys only from main
The site is for people with access to this repository only
settings.source: MASTER-PLAN, Who can see it; publish guard

settings.why: Only the reviewed workflow deploys, never a branch push
One login does all the work, so one admin, organization owners included; counts only, never names. The first read with the key confirms it
Contributors work from forks, so no one holds direct access as an outside collaborator
No workflow or service uses a deploy key, and a key sits outside the ruleset's actors
A webhook without a secret can be faked
A webhook must verify TLS
Every secret this repository can use is named by a workflow on main; an unused key is a leak waiting to happen. Names only, never values
settings.source: GitHub secure use reference, least privilege

settings.why: No secret older than a year, Dependabot secrets included

A repository-level secret reaches pull request workflows on any branch. Only the review key needs that; every other secret lives in a main-only environment. A name no workflow on main uses is kept as unreferenced, never as itself
No organization secret is shared into this repository
settings.source: GitHub secure use reference, least privilege

settings.why: Dependabot pull requests read only Dependabot secrets, so the review key is stored there too, and nothing else: dependabot.yml uses no private registry. A name no workflow uses is kept as unreferenced
Every member signs in with two factors
Membership alone grants no access to a repository
A copy of this code can't land in a public repository by a member's click
Backs up the repository's own forking setting
No member can publish a public Pages site; this site must stay private
No member can make this repository public or internal
Organization webhooks receive this repository's events too
As above, over TLS

Distinct products with a product-level $0 budget that stops usage, at organization or enterprise scope, so per-SKU budgets on one product or a budget on some other repository can't pass: the worst case is that CI pauses, never a bill
Actions, where nearly all of this repository's spend is, has its own $0 stop budget
No budget above $0 or without the stop; spending is the owner's call
settings.source: MASTER-PLAN, Enterprise upgrade; CLAUDE.md, billing goes to the owner

not_scored.why: GitHub Secret Protection is paid on a private repository and is not being bought; CI's gitleaks scan covers it
Part of the same paid product
GitHub Code Security is paid on a private repository and is not being bought

not_scored.source: GitHub REST API, 404 on a private repository

not_scored.why: Forking is off at both repository and organization, so a fork pull request can't exist
Variables are not secrets, and listing them returns values such as an account id; only CLAUDE_ENABLED is read, through the workflow's vars context, as true or false
Listing them needs Codespaces secrets write, which a read-only key can't hold; Codespaces isn't used
not_scored.source: GitHub docs, permissions for fine-grained tokens

not_scored.why: A repository setting changed and changed back between reads can't be seen: the audit log needs a classic token and ruleset history needs write access. Rulesets are covered through their updated_at
not_scored.source: GitHub docs, permissions for fine-grained tokens
